newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia seeks to boost exports to Iran.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia seeks to boost exports to Iran.

text.p: Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said on Monday Indonesia aimed to boost exports to Iran in bid to narrow its trade deficit with Tehran.

Speaking after accompanying Iranian Post and Telecomunication Minister Mohammad Gharazi to a meeting with President Suharto, Ariwibowo said two-way trade totalled $389 million in 1995, compared with $280 million in 1994.
He said Indonesia exported goods worth $132 million in 1995, while imports amounted to $257 million.
Indonesian exports to Iran included pulp and paper, steel and rubber, while imports were mainly crude oil.
"We expect bilateral trade to increase to around $500 million this year and we agreed to boost it to $1 billion in the next couple years," Ariwibowo said.
Gharazi told reporters that there was a big potential for both countries to improve bilateral trade.
"I think it will be easy to reach the target of $1 billion in annual trade," he said.
